universalAnswers.whatHappened: Five developments from September 9–16 changed the safety debate, school contract scope and consumer AI conversations.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A selective Weekly synthesis separating proposals, provider findings, signed terms and rollouts.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Primary proposal, provider report and announcements, signed agreement, and the prior LAiDIES Weekly.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: No claim that outside reviewers are operating, school coverage is automatic, misuse intent or weapon completion is proven, or rollouts establish accuracy.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: Parents and everyday tool users can ask which assurance applies to their exact product, account or conversation.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: School communities, people affected by AI misuse, voice-tool users and people who choose an advertiser-sponsored chat.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The report, agreement and announcements are public; implementation and rollout remain bounded as stated.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Reviewer operation, school uptake, feature availability and outcomes require later evidence.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Ask what is operating, who or what is covered and what evidence can be inspected.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Who does this cover, and how will we know it works?

legal-policy.legalStatus: A signed opt-in agreement defines protections for covered educational AI products; it is not a universal law or automatic rule for every Microsoft product.
legal-policy.jurisdiction: The agreement is available to US education customers that request it for a covered educational AI product.
legal-policy.parties: Microsoft, the American Federation of Teachers and the United Federation of Teachers announced the terms; an eligible school customer chooses whether to opt in.
legal-policy.allegationVsFinding: The agreement text establishes contractual promises and exclusions; the Weekly does not claim tested compliance, school uptake or proven outcomes.
legal-policy.currentEffect: A participating school can request the protections in its customer agreement, including restrictions on covered-data advertising and generally on model training.
legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Public evidence does not yet establish how many schools opt in, which named school products qualify or how the terms perform in practice.
legal-policy.nextMilestone: Watch for school contract uptake, product-specific coverage decisions and evidence that the promised protections are being implemented.

safety-incident.incident: Anthropic reports surveillance and dual-use biology activity observed on its systems.
safety-incident.harm: The report identifies potential for harm without establishing harmful intent or a completed biological weapon.
safety-incident.affectedPeople: People targeted by surveillance and communities potentially exposed to misuse.
safety-incident.failedControl: The Weekly does not infer a particular failed control beyond what the provider report states.
safety-incident.responsibility: Anthropic owns its report and system controls; public evidence is needed to assess implementation.
safety-incident.confirmedUnknown: Observed provider activity is reported; intent, completed weapon and prevalence across all AI use are not established.
safety-incident.remediation: The story connects the report to demands for inspectable outside review without claiming resolution.
safety-incident.recurrenceRisk: Dual-use research and surveillance remain concerns while implementation evidence is incomplete.

model-tool-release.productRange: Gemini 3.8 Live/Extended Thinking and OpenAI Sponsored Agents.
model-tool-release.newCapabilities: Continued spoken interaction during processing, and an optional advertiser-sponsored conversation after an ad click.
model-tool-release.bestFitTasks: Ordinary voice planning and low-stakes product questions.
model-tool-release.notFor: A fluent result does not prove task accuracy; a seller chat is not independent shopping advice.
model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: Check a finished packing list manually or stay in the original independent ChatGPT conversation.
model-tool-release.availability: Google rollout and subscription limits apply; OpenAI describes a select-US-advertiser test.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: Google names subscriptions for Docs/Gmail/Keep features; OpenAI does not state a user tier boundary for the test.
model-tool-release.costBoundary: No user price claim is made.
model-tool-release.limitations: Provider announcements only; no independent outcome evidence.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: One packing-list example explains the need to inspect a finished result.
model-tool-release.vendorEvidenceBoundary: Every availability and behavior claim is attributed or bounded to the provider source.

translation.newsVersionExact: On September 12, Anthropic chief Dario Amodei called for slowing improvements to the most capable AI systems so safety work can keep up.
translation.mechanismExact: Schools must opt in, and the definition excludes general-purpose productivity, communications and search products even when schools use them.
translation.familiarExampleExact: If you talk through a packing list for a weekend away, check that the final list kept the details you gave it.
